title: $f^*\circ p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $f^*$ be the pullback of
abelian pro-étale sheaves along $f$, and let
$p_X^*=\pi_X^*\circ p^*$, $p_Y^*=\pi_Y^*\circ p^*$ be the inverse images from
the point ([det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image],
[sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]). Since $\Spec\Z$ is terminal,
$\pi_Y\circ f=\pi_X$. The natural isomorphism
$$
f^*\circ p_Y^*=f^*\pi_Y^*p^*\ \cong\ (\pi_Y\circ f)^*p^*=\pi_X^*p^*=p_X^*
$$
is $p^*$ composed with the inverse of the composition isomorphism
$(\pi_Y\circ f)^*\cong f^*\circ\pi_Y^*$ of
[det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image], followed by the identification
$(\pi_Y\circ f)^*=\pi_X^*$.

It is a monoidal natural isomorphism for the strong monoidal structures of
$f^*\circ p_Y^*$ and $p_X^*$ and the tensor products of
[sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor].

proof.text: The comparison natural isomorphism is exactly [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso]. Its compatibility with the tensor unit and tensor comparison maps is [lem-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-monoidal]. Therefore these two cited declarations provide the required natural isomorphism and its monoidal structure.

Using [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp] with $h_1=f$ and $h_2=\pi_Y$, the right-adjoint composition identifies $p_*\pi_{Y*}f_*$ with $p_* (\pi_Y\circ f)_*$, and the terminal identification $\pi_Y\circ f=\pi_X$ gives $p_*\pi_{X*}$. The right-adjoint description in [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] then evaluates this comparison at a sheaf $G$ on $X$ and a profinite set $S$ as $G(Y[S]\times_Y X)\cong G(X[S])$, induced by the canonical iterated-fibre-product identification $X\times_Y Y[S]\cong X[S]$.
